recap.workouts:
Three for three, and the one that mattered went right. CrossFit: Lake at [FITNESS], cruised exactly as called — 1h13, avg HR 116, max 161, RPE 5, and your note was one word: Easy. That is what protecting a tune looks like. Lifting (upper pull + triceps): lat pulldown 180x12/12, barbell row 75x12, free-bar curl 40x12/12, face pull 80x20/20, overhead triceps ext 110x12/12 — every load held at the deload dose, every set at or over the top of its range, zero creep.

CT31 — BIKE TUNE, 60 min, and your note was: I followed exactly what you told me to do. You did, and the data says so. Warm-up honest: 5' at 136 W, then 15' Z2 at 172 W, HR sitting 133 into the block. The 24' block, five minutes at a time: 0-5' at 220 W, HR climbing 133 to 149 · 5-10' at 222 W, HR 151 · 10-15' at 233 W, HR 156 · 15-20' at 239 W, HR 158 · 20-24' at 240 W, HR 159. Mean output 229.5 W against a 215-230 W target — top of the band — with watts held between 218 and 242 for the whole block (steadiness CV 3.8%: genuinely flat riding, not surging).

The heart-rate story is the good part. You settled at 142 a minute in, and the last nine minutes plateaued at 158-159 while you were pushing 239-240 W — the curve went flat and stayed flat, and it never reached 162. Raw drift across the block was +7.1 bpm, but that is bought drift: you raised power from 224 W to 238 W between halves, and watts-per-beat actually IMPROVED (decoupling -0.5%). Aerobically coupled, no fade, no runaway. The tail was clean too — 16' of Z2 and cool-down at 145 W, HR back down to 123.
recap.takeaways:
1) TUNE RESULT — valid, and the anchors moved. FTP 225 -> 236 W. Bike LTHR 162 -> 159. Medium confidence. VO2max estimate 51.1 -> 53.3. One honest caveat: the +5% per-tune cap binds here, so 236 is deliberately the conservative number — the raw read wanted more, which means there is likely a little still in the tank for the Week 12 retest. Run anchors untouched; Thursday's RT19 owns those.

2) The execution earned it, and I want to be plain about that. Holding 158-159 bpm for nine minutes at 240 W, with watts-per-beat rising, is a fitness signal rather than a lucky day. You asked whether I'm proud — yes. You also closed out last week's mess: the analyzer had rejected exactly this ride pattern because its cleanliness gate assumed flat output; that gate is now power-normalised, and your execution was right all along.

3) ADAPT: no-op, and correctly so. CT31 EXECUTED (87.8% compliance, full block delivered, paired cleanly to the planned session), class kept easy, lifting exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week changes.

4) Practical, starting tomorrow: the bike zones rescale. Z2 is now 165-196 W (was 158-187), Z3 threshold 222-248 W, Z4 248-283 W. Ride the new numbers, not the old ones — and note that an easy day at a higher Z2 is still an easy day, not a harder one.
